sentences.text: Caupedactylus had a skull approximately forty-six centimeters long and a wingspan estimated at 3.3 meters, making it the largest known tapejarine.
Its snout features a crest on the premaxilla that extends both forward and backward, yet this structure is very thin, measuring about half a millimeter at its upper part.
With a wingspan of 3.3 meters, this creature holds the record for the largest known tapejarine.
Despite its impressive size, the skull crest is remarkably thin, measuring only half a millimeter at its thickest point.
The genus Caupedactylus was first named and described by Alexander Wilhelm Armin Kellner in 2013.
The holotype specimen MN 4726-V dates to about 110 million years ago from the Albian stage of the Romualdo Formation in the Araripe basin.
This fossil specimen was extracted from chalkstone using an acid bath.
A 2019 phylogenetic analysis by Kellner and colleagues recovered Caupedactylus as the basalmost tapejarine.
Caupedactylus lived between 119.57 and 113.2 million years ago during the Aptian stage.
